===Etymology 1===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:cool<ety:inh<ang:cōl<id:cool>>>|id=adj|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|cool}}, from {{inh|en|ang|cōl|id=cool|t=cool, cold, tranquil, calm}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kōl(ī)}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kōluz|t=cool}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*kalaną|t=to be cold, to freeze}}, {{der|en|ine-pro|*gel-|t=to be cold, to freeze}}.
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|frr|kool}}, {{m|frr|koul}}, {{m|frr|kuul}}, {{m|frr|kölj}}, {{m|frr|kööl|t=cold}}, {{cog|stq|köil|t=cool}}, {{cog|fy|koel|t=cool}}, {{cog|cim|khuul|t=chilly, cool}}, {{cog|nl|koel|t=cool}}, {{cog|de|kühl|t=cool}}, {{cog|nds|köhl|t=cool}}, {{cog|lb|kill|t=cool}}, {{cog|wym|kił|t=cool}}; also {{cog|la|gelū}}, {{m|la|gelum}}, {{m|la|gelus|t=frost; chill, cold}}, {{cog|be|хо́лад|t=cold}}, {{cog|bg|хлад|t=chill, coolness}}, {{cog|cs|chlad|t=cold}}, {{cog|mk|лад|t=shade; coolness}}, {{cog|pl|chłód|t=cold}}, {{cog|ru,uk|хо́лод|t=cold}}, {{cog|sh|хла̑д}}, {{m|sh|hlȃd|t=shade}}, {{cog|sa|जड|t=cold; stiff}}, {{m|sa|जल|t=water}}. Related to {{m|en|cold}}.

====Adjective====
{{en-adj|er}}
[[File:Warm and cool colors.svg|thumb|'''cool''' colors]]

# {{senseid|en|temperature}} Of a mildly low temperature.
#: {{syn|en|chilly}}
#: {{ant|en|lukewarm|tepid|warm}}
#: {{ux|en|I like '''cool''' weather the most 'cause it's not too hot to wear a jacket but I won't be too cold in my shorts.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=The day was '''cool''' and snappy for August, and the Rise all green with a lavish nature. Now we plunged into a deep shade with the boughs lacing each other overhead, and crossed dainty, rustic bridges over the cold trout-streams, the boards giving back the clatter of our horses' feet:{{...}}.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=Ashley Strickland|title=Astronomers discover nearby six-planet solar system with ‘pristine configuration’|magazine=w:CNN|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2023/11/29/world/six-exoplanets-resonance-scn|date=2023-11-29|passage=Many exoplanets have been found orbiting dwarf stars that are much '''cooler''' and smaller than our sun, such as the famed TRAPPIST-1 system and its seven planets, announced in 2017.}}
# Allowing or suggesting heat [[relief]].
#: {{ux|en|Linen has made '''cool''' and breathable clothing for millennia.}}
#* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=2|passage=Now that she had rested and had fed from the luncheon tray Mrs. Broome had just removed, she had reverted to her normal gaiety.&nbsp; She looked '''cool''' in a grey tailored cotton dress with a terracotta scarf and shoes and her hair a black silk helmet.}}
# Of a color, in the range of violet to green.
#: {{ant|en|warm}}
#: {{ux|en|If you have a reddish complexion, you should mainly wear '''cool''' colors.}}
# {{senseid|en|calm}}{{lb|en|of a person}} Not showing emotion; [[calm]] and in control of oneself.
#: {{syn|en|distant|phlegmatic|standoffish|unemotional}}
#: {{ant|en|passionate}}
#: {{ux|en|Be '''cool'''. There's no need to panic.}}
# {{senseid|en|unenthusiastic; lukewarm; skeptical}} [[unenthusiastic|Unenthusiastic]]; [[lukewarm]]; [[skeptical]].
#: {{syn|en|chilly|lukewarm|tepid}}
#: {{ant|en|warm}}
#: {{ux|en|His proposals had a '''cool''' reception.}}
# {{senseid|en|calmly audacious}} {{lb|en|obsolete}} Calmly [[audacious]].
#* {{RQ:Hawthorne Scarlet Letter|chapter=Hester at her Needle|passage=Its '''cool''' stare of familiarity was intolerable.}}
#* {{quote-text|en|date=Feb 27 1860|url=https://www.abrahamlincolnonline.org/lincoln/speeches/cooper.htm|author=Abe Lincoln|title=Cooper Union address|passage=In that supposed event, you say, you will destroy the Union; and then, you say, the great crime of having destroyed it will be upon us! That is '''cool'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Alcott Little Women|part=1|chapter=13|passage="Well, that's '''cool'''," said Laurie to himself, "to have a picnic and never ask me!"}}
# {{senseid|en|of money}} {{non-gloss|Applied facetiously to a sum of money, commonly as if to give emphasis to the largeness of the amount.}}
#* {{RQ:Fielding Tom Jones
|passage=Who will lend me a '''cool''' hundred.}}
#* {{RQ:Dickens Great Expectations|volume=III|chapter=XVIII|page=303|passage=But she had wrote out a little coddleshell in her own hand a day or two afore the accident, leaving a '''cool''' four thousand to Mr. Matthew Pocket.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1900|author=w:Dora Sigerson Shorter|title=Transmigration|passage=You remember Bulger, don't you? You lost a '''cool''' hundred to him one night here over the cards, eh?}}
#* {{quote-av|en|date=1944 November 28|writer=w:Irving Brecher; w:Fred F. Finklehoffe|title=w:Meet Me in St. Louis|publisher=Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer|passage=My father was talking to the World's Fair Commission yesterday, and they estimate it's going to cost a '''cool''' fifty million.}}
# {{senseid|en|knowing how to behave astutely; popular with others}} {{lb|en|informal|of a person}} Knowing what to do and how to behave; behaving with [[effortless]] and [[enviable]] style and [[panache]]; considered [[popular]] by others.
#: {{ant|en|awkward|uncool}}
#* {{RQ:Dickens Pickwick Papers|chapter=28|page=284|passage={{...|Another crack of the whip, and on they speed, at a smart gallop, the horses tossing their heads and rattling the harness as if in exhilaration at the rapidity of the motion,}} while the coachman holding whip and reins in one hand, takes off his hat with the other, and resting it on his knees, pulls out his handkerchief, and wipes his forehead, partly because he has a habit of doing it, and partly because it's as well to shew the passengers how '''cool''' he is, and what an easy thing it is to drive four-in-hand, when you have had as much practice as he has.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2000|author=Malcolm Gladwell|title=The Tipping Point|passage=Maggie the au pair, and Pam P. on the school bus and Billy G. with his Grateful Dead records were all deeply '''cool''' people. But they weren’t '''cool''' because they smoked. They smoked because they were '''cool'''.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=December 27, 2017| title=The Guardian view on Prince Harry: the monarchy’s best insurance policy| work=the Guardian| url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2017/dec/27/the-guardian-view-on-prince-harry-the-monarchys-best-insurance-policy| passage=He managed to conduct interviews with the least '''cool''' global figure – his father, Prince Charles – and the most '''cool''', Barack Obama, in a way that allowed them both to look as good as they could.}}
#* {{RQ:NYT|author=Christina Caron|title=What Makes Someone Cool? A New Study Offers Clues.|date=2025-06-30|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/30/well/mind/cool-people-traits-study.html|passage=Is there a secret sauce that helps explain why people as different as David Bowie, Samuel L. Jackson and Charli XCX all seem so self-assured and, well, '''cool'''? A new study suggests that there are six specific traits that these people tend to have in common: '''Cool''' people are largely perceived to be extroverted, hedonistic, powerful, adventurous, open and autonomous.}}
# {{senseid|en|fashionable; trendy; hip}} {{lb|en|informal|originally|AAVE}} [[fashionable|Fashionable]]; [[trendy]]; [[hip#English:_trendy|hip]].
#: {{syn|en|à la mode|fashionable|in fashion|modish|stylish|happening|hip|in|trendy}}
#: {{ant|en|démodé|old hat|out|out of fashion}}
#* {{quote-av|en|year=1953|writers=w:Dalton Trumbo; w:Ian McLellan Hunter; w:John Dighton|title=w:Roman Holiday|role=Mario Delani|actor=Paolo Carlini|passage=You be nice without long hair. Now it's '''cool''', hmm?}}
#* '''2008''', Lou Schuler, "Foreward", ''in'' Nate Green, ''Built for Show'', page xii
#*: The fact that I was middle-aged, bald, married, and raising girls instead of chasing them didn't really bother me. Muscles are '''cool''' at any age.
# {{senseid|en|all right; acceptable; good}} {{lb|en|informal}} [[all right|All right]]; [[acceptable]]; [[good]].
#: {{syn|en|acceptable|all right|OK}}
#: {{ant|en|not cricket|q1=UK|not on|unacceptable}}
#: {{ux|en|Is it '''cool''' if I sleep here tonight?}}
#* {{quote-song|en|lyricist={{w|Bobby Pickett|Bobby "Boris" Pickett}}, Lenny Capizzi|title=w:Monster Mash|artist=Bobby (Boris) Pickett and The Crypt-Kickers|year=1962|text=Now everything's '''cool''', Drac's a part of the band / And my Monster Mash is the hit of the land / For you, the living, this Mash was meant too / When you get to my door, tell them Boris sent you.}}
# {{lb|en|informal}} Very interesting or exciting.
#: {{syn|en|awesome|neat}}
#: {{ux|en|I think astronomy is really '''cool'''.}}
# {{lb|en|informal}} Followed by [[with]]: able to tolerate.
#: {{syn|en|easy|fine|not [[bothered]]|not [[fussed]]}}
#: {{ant|en|bothered|upset}}
#: {{ux|en|I'm completely '''cool''' with my girlfriend leaving me.}}
# {{lb|en|informal}} Of a pair of people, Having good relations.
#: {{ux|en|We're '''cool''', right?}}

===Etymology 2===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:colen<ety:inh<ang:cōlian>>|id=verb|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|colen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|cōlian||to cool, grow cold, be cold}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kōlēn||to become cold}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gel-||to freeze}}.

Cognate with {{cog|nl|koelen||to cool}}, {{cog|de|kühlen||to cool}}, {{cog|sv|kyla||to cool, refrigerate}}. Also partially from {{inh|en|enm|kelen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|cēlan||to cool, be cold, become cold}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kōlijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kōlijaną||to cool}}, altered to resemble the adjective {{m|en|cool}}. See {{m|en|keel}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive|literally}} To lose heat, to get [[colder]].
#: {{syn|en|cool down}}
#: {{ant|en|warm#Verb|warm up|heat#Verb|heat up}}
#: {{hypo|en|freeze#Verb}}
#: {{ux|en|I like to let my tea '''cool''' before drinking it so I don't burn my tongue.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|literally}} To [[make]] cooler, less warm.
#: {{syn|en|chill#Verb|cool down|refrigerate|;|deheat|qq4=rare}}
#: {{ant|en|warm#Verb|warm up|heat#Verb|heat up}}
#: {{hypo|en|freeze#Verb}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Luke|16|24|text=Send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and '''cool''' my tongue.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|figuratively}} To become less intense, e.g. less [[amicable]] or [[passionate]].
#: {{ux|en|Relations '''cooled''' between the USA and the USSR after 1980.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|figuratively}} To make less intense, e.g. less [[amicable]] or [[passionate]].
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Othello|I|iii|passage=We have reason to '''cool''' our raging motions, our carnal stings, our unbitted lusts.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|slang|dated}} To [[kill#Verb|kill]], [[murder#Verb|murder]].
#* '''1965''', "Sex Jungle" (narrated in ''Perversion for Profit'')
#*: Maybe he would die. That would mean I had murdered him. I smiled, trying the idea on for size. One of the things that always had cheesed me a little was that I had no kills to my credit. I'd been in plenty of rumbles, but somehow, I'd never '''cooled''' anyone. Well maybe now I had my first one. I couldn't feel very proud of skulling an old man, but at least I could say that I'd scored. That was a big kick.
#* {{quote-book|en|author=w:Piri Thomas|title=w:Down These Mean Streets|publisher=w:Alfred A. Knopf|location=New York, N.Y.|year=1967|page=31|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/downthesemeanstr0000thom/page/31/mode/1up|passage=Big-mouth got up as fast as he could, and I was thinking how much heart he had. But I ran toward him like my life depended on it; I wanted to '''cool''' him.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|AAVE|slang}} To [[relax#Verb|relax]], [[hang out#Verb|hang out]].
#: {{syn|en|bool<qq:slang>}}
#* {{quote-song|en|artist=w:Ice-T|title=w:6 in the Mornin'|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pzCGPlDgbgU|year=1986|passage=Seen my homeboys '''coolin'''{{'}} way way out / Told 'em bout my mornin' cold bugged' em out}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=w:Paul Beatty|title=Tuff: A Novel|location=New York, N.Y.|publisher=w:Anchor Books|year=2000|year_published=2001|page=223|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/tuffnovel0000beat/page/223/mode/1up|isbn=978-0-385-72111-0|passage="What up, kid?" ¶ "'''Coolin'''{{'}}."}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=w:Courttia Newland|title=The Scholar: A West Side Story|location=London|publisher=[[w:Abacus (imprint)|Abacus]]|year=1997|page=207|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/scholarwestsides0000newl/page/207/mode/1up|isbn=0-349-10844-7|passage='<nowiki/>''Asbestos''? Raa, dat's a dangerous t'ing boy, dat ain't good. You know what though, you guys should min' yourselves walkin' street star, dere's bere nutters about. I know you're in a crew but boy can't you jus' '''cool''' at someone's house?'}}
